hypotheses.mechanism: The only single-variable public step above the wall is x138 = thtennant readmit-v1 (0.946) + V1284 head (0.953, +0.007). The competing explanations are ruled out by public evidence. Eric (77th) tried heuristic sub-voxel peak refinement: +0.0078 on 12 local videos, -0.002 on the LB twice. Le Quang Canh's constant offset lost 0.0031. flow2, which denoises velocity, was neutral (0.947). So the gain comes from the LEARNED, feature-conditioned per-node displacement, not from de-quantisation as such. I inspected the public v1284_head.pt (CC0, 34 KB). Under unit-normal inputs its offsets have a median norm of 0.40 um with per-axis sd z 0.34 / y 0.17 / x 0.21 um, and the z output row carries the largest weight (0.25 vs 0.14 / 0.16). These are sub-lattice corrections: peaks live on an isotropic 1.625 um feature grid (UNet ds 1,4,4), and 98.3% of pre-linefit edge lengths in edges_exp39.parquet are exact lattice distances. The head was fitted on only 4,136 detection-GT pairs from 20 movies. Its author: the 4-movie version was 14.9% WORSE and the 20-movie version -10.4% (16/20 held-out movies better), 'the null was volume'. Our lab has ~129k annotated GT edges (TP 122,151 + FN 6,732) over 199 videos, i.e. >= 30x the pairs. Second defect: x138 applies the head to unet_out = _unet_acc/_nv, the 8-view TTA-averaged features (EDGE_FEATURE_TTA=1), while the stored mean/scale come from x107's capture, whose TTA setting is unknown. Averaged features have lower variance, so the standardised inputs and the offsets may be systematically shrunk or distorted. A head refitted on our exact TTA-averaged features removes that mismatch and uses 30x the data.
hypotheses.change: (1) Capture kernel on Kaggle 2xT4 (x138's own V1284_MODE=capture hook, extended). For EVERY raw peak, dump the lattice coords (t,z,y,x) plus the public-head offset. For peaks within 4 um of a GT node, also dump the 224-d TTA-averaged feature vector (fp16) and the GT displacement in um. Run on ~60 videos stratified over both embryos and the 44b6 leak groups (~3-4 GPU h over 2 GPUs), all 199 if quota allows. (2) CPU training: (a) the same 224->32->3 MLP with bounded output (<= 2 um); (b) 27-neighbour context 864->64->3; (c) ridge baseline. Huber loss on the 3D displacement in um, GroupKFold by leak group / embryo, no embryo id as input. (3) Ship as a drop-in replacement of v1284_head.pt (same dict: state_dict, mean, scale), so the port needs zero code change.
hypotheses.upper_bound: Public mapping: -10.4% centre error <-> +0.007 LB (one run, +-0.003). If the score scales roughly linearly with error reduction, going from -10% to -20% is worth <= +0.007 more. Edge-side hard ceiling = FN classes decided by localisation at matching/relink time: a_linefit 353 + u_diverted/v_taken 1,149 (oracle +0.016). So <= +0.016 local, realistically a fraction of it.
hypotheses.lab_test: (1) Held-out (by leak group) mean 3D matched distance to GT per embryo: lattice vs public head vs v2. The public head's own held-out gain is -10.4% vs lattice. Success = v2 at least 5% below the public head on BOTH 44b6 and 6bba. (2) Lab replay: replace the node coords in friend A's cache by lattice + offset, joined on (stem,t,z,y,x); the pipeline is deterministic (exp46 sha256 parity). Re-run post-processing on SELECTION, then ONE CONFIRMATION run: v2 vs public head >= +0.002, each embryo >= +0.001, gains on >= 55% of videos per embryo, 90% CI > 0. Caveat: cached edge probabilities stay from the integer gather, so report the relink/matching effect only.
hypotheses.expected_gain: +0.001..+0.004 public over the ported public head. Arithmetic: error reduction improving from 10% to 13-16% gives 1/3 to 1/2 of the observed +0.007 step.
hypotheses.transfer_risk: Features come from a detector trained on all 199 train videos, so the head can learn in-sample residuals. The public head carries the same caveat and still transferred (+0.007). The 44b6 annotation z bias (dz ~ -0.57 um) is embryo-dependent and may differ on the hidden embryos, so: features only, no embryo id; select on the per-embryo held-out gain; keep the public head as fallback if v2 wins on one embryo only.
hypotheses.not_closed_because: It is not a detector fine-tune (detector frozen), not TTA, not a weight soup, and not the port itself (the port reuses the public 20-movie weights). It is a new learned second stage with 30x the data, plus a fix for a train/inference feature-normalisation mismatch.

hypotheses.mechanism: megayak's public notebook ('The 0.966 notebooks used a patched metric bug', appendix) audited every one of the 151 train GT divisions: the shipped safe-division gates leave only 35 reachable. The divergence threshold of 2.25 um sits at the median of real divisions and symmetry 0.6 at ~p60 ('coin flips'). Opening the gates alone loses (0.9508 -> 0.9341), because the geometry ranker spends the ~5 slots per frame on duplicates. On our graph the gate statistics are computed from lattice positions: 98.3% of pre-linefit lengths are exact 1.625 um lattice distances, i.e. about 0.66 um of quantisation noise per axis per point. The divergence (difference of two sister distances across frames) then carries sd ~1.3 um against a 2.25 um threshold, and the symmetry ratio |d1-d2|/mean at d ~4.6 um carries sd ~0.2 against 0.6. A large share of the gate decisions is therefore quantisation noise, not biology. Forum: Lime1123 says divisions need ~3 um accuracy even with the 7 um metric (kevin park: 39% of his division nodes > 3 um off). Our numbers: public J_div 0.36 (probe 26 vs probe 28), local TP 23 / FP 43 / FN 128; the DaughterNet insertion added-fork precision is 27% vs the 26.5% break-even. With head-refined float coordinates (x138 port) the geometric gates become informative: duplicates have divergence ~0 and would separate from real divisions, and the insertion geometry gets more precise.
hypotheses.change: After the port, compute every safe-division gate feature (parent distance, sister distance, symmetry, divergence, existing-child distance) and the DaughterNet-insertion geometry on head-refined coordinates. Re-select SAFE_DIV_DIVERGE_UM {1.0, 1.5, 2.25, 3.0} x SAFE_DIV_SISTER_SYMMETRY_TAU {0.4, 0.6, 0.8, off}. Replace the ascending parent_dist + 0.15*sister_dist ranking with DaughterNet p (already scored for all 1,012,255 exported nodes), keeping the per-frame and global caps. Post-processing only.
hypotheses.upper_bound: If de-quantised gates raise the reachable set from 35 to ~50 of 151 at the current precision (23/66 = 0.35): local TP 23->33, FP 43->61, FN 128->118, so J_div 0.119 -> 0.156 = +0.0037 score. Scaled to the public J_div of 0.36: 0.36 x 1.31 = 0.47, i.e. +0.011 ceiling.
hypotheses.lab_test: Step 0 (CPU, minutes, as soon as the capture of head-v2-199 exists): megayak-style gate audit on the 151 GT divisions using the predicted parent/daughter nodes, with lattice vs refined coordinates. Readout = reachable count per gate; go on only if reachable rises by >= 8. Step 1: SELECTION grid (16 gate configs x DaughterNet ranking on/off), then ONE CONFIRMATION run with the pre-registered division gate: >= +0.002 overall and >= +0.001 per embryo, net division TP >= +3, added-fork precision >= 0.31, adj_edge within 0.001.
hypotheses.expected_gain: +0.001..+0.004 public (J_div +0.01..+0.04). The mid case (+5 net public TP at precision ~0.45) gives about +0.002.
hypotheses.transfer_risk: Only 151 train divisions, and local deltas are 1-4 events (noise; the L2 v1 selection gain of +0.0044 shrank to +0.0010 on confirmation). Forks below 26.5% precision lose on the public board. The head offsets in the lab come from in-sample features. The public embryo seems to have easier divisions (J 0.36 public vs 0.12 local), so relative gains may not scale.
hypotheses.not_closed_because: DivNet veto and the division pair model are closed, and B20 settled the gate thresholds, but only on lattice coordinates. The new mechanism is that gate statistics were dominated by 1.625 um quantisation noise, which the float-coordinate port removes. The DaughterNet ranking is ours and has been LB-positive once (probe 28).

hypotheses.mechanism: Linefit smoothing (weight 0.8, window 2) is the largest post-processing stage: B28 on 12 videos measured 0.9001 with it vs 0.8856 off (+0.0145); w0.5 0.8948 and w1.0 0.8955. That optimum was selected on lattice inputs. In edges_exp39.parquet, 98.3% of pre-linefit edge lengths are exact multiples of the 1.625 um lattice vs 0.9% after linefit, and 22% of TP edges (26,365 / 122,151) have a pre-linefit length of exactly 0. Much of what linefit buys is therefore de-quantisation. Once the x138 head (median 0.40 um learned offsets, float coordinates end-to-end) removes part of that noise, the bias-variance optimum moves toward less smoothing, and w0.8 mostly adds bias on turning or accelerating cells. The FN anatomy (exp39 + edge filter, validated against the official scorer) already attributes 353 FN (5.8%, class a_linefit) to linefit displacement on lattice coordinates. x138 ships w0.8 / win2 unchanged in its only version, so no public notebook has re-selected linefit for float input.
hypotheses.change: On the ported stack (exp48 + head), run a grid over OUTPUT_LINEFIT_WEIGHT {0.3, 0.5, 0.65, 0.8} x OUTPUT_LINEFIT_WINDOW {1, 2, 3}. Add a turn-aware variant: halve or skip smoothing at a node whose second difference |x_{t+1} - 2x_t + x_{t-1}| exceeds k x 1.8 um (k 1.0 / 1.5), and never extend the window across a fork. Topology unchanged, output coordinates only.
hypotheses.upper_bound: Recovering all 353 a_linefit FN with FP unchanged: J 122,151/135,729 = 0.89997 -> 122,504/135,729 = 0.90256, i.e. +0.0026. The B28 curve (w0.5 -0.0053, off -0.0145 on lattice) shows that moving the optimum is worth a few thousandths either way.
hypotheses.lab_test: Needs the refined per-node coordinates from the head-v2-199 capture (public-head offsets for every raw peak). Lab replay on SELECTION with 12 + 4 configs, then ONE CONFIRMATION run. Success: best config >= +0.002 vs head + w0.8, each embryo >= +0.001, gains on >= 55% of videos per embryo, and the a_linefit FN count falls. A pilot on lattice coordinates is uninformative (that is B28).
hypotheses.expected_gain: 0..+0.002 public. The main value is protecting the port from a hidden -0.001..-0.003 double-smoothing loss.
hypotheses.transfer_risk: Low to medium. Linefit is geometry-only (no learned score), and post-processing settings chosen locally have transferred on this LB (hikaggler, Justin CH123). The risk is that the lab's head offsets are in-sample, so their noise may be understated, which would bias the choice toward too little smoothing. Choose the more conservative of any tied configs.
hypotheses.not_closed_because: B28 closed the linefit grid on lattice input only. The input distribution changes with the float-coordinate port, which nobody (x138 included) re-selected for, and the turn/fork-aware stop is a new rule rather than a knob value.

hypotheses.mechanism: The motion relink (which replaces the ILP edge set) runs its Hungarian on lattice positions, with velocity = source_pos - prev_pos from a single frame (weight 0.5). In edges_exp39.parquet, relink_raw_um / len_pre_um are lattice-exact for 98.3% of edges. The velocity quantisation noise is ~0.66 um per axis (~1.15 um 3D) against a 1.8 um median true step, consistent with Le's 'velocity extrapolation picks the true child 0/381 times'. Among evaluable edges, FP edges have an alternative target within one lattice step (|margin| <= 1.63 um) in 12.6% of cases vs 1.5% for TP, and the FP pre-linefit length median is 3.25 um vs 2.30 um for TP. So a visible slice of FP comes from near-ties that lattice geometry cannot resolve. The x138 head refines only detector peaks, and only by ~0.4 um. Synthetic gap nodes and the velocity estimate stay noisy. Temporal pre-smoothing of the ILP tracks gives sub-lattice decision positions at zero GPU cost, and it is testable NOW in the CPU lab without any capture.
hypotheses.change: Before motion_relink_edges, close_single_frame_gaps, gap2 recovery, safe divisions and the edge filter's re-link step, compute 'decision positions' = linefit (window 2, weight wd in {0.5, 0.8, 1.0}) over ILP single-chain neighbourhoods. Use them for raw/motion distances and for velocity (difference of smoothed positions). Output coordinates are unchanged (the final linefit on the output graph as now). Transfer-control variant: build the chains from mutual nearest neighbours within 3 um in adjacent frames instead of ILP edges, so it is network-free.
hypotheses.upper_bound: 865 near-tie FP (12.6% of 6,846). Fixing half of them, each converting FP->TP and removing one FN: J 0.89997 -> 122,583/(122,583 + 6,414 + 6,300) = 0.9060, +0.006. Realistic 10-25% of them: +0.001..+0.003 local.
hypotheses.lab_test: A replay.py patch, run on Kaggle CPU lab kernels. SELECTION grid (3 wd x {ILP chains, mutual-NN chains} x {relink only, all gates}), then ONE CONFIRMATION run with the standard gate (>= +0.002, each embryo >= +0.001, >= 55% of videos per embryo, 90% CI > 0). Readouts: the near-tie FP count and the b_swap / b_u_diverted / b_v_taken FN counts from fn_anatomy.py. Adopt only if the network-free variant also passes.
hypotheses.expected_gain: 0..+0.002 public (local +0.001..+0.003, discounted for the transfer evidence below).
hypotheses.transfer_risk: HIGH, with direct counter-evidence: Eric's heuristic sub-voxel refinement gave +0.0078 locally and -0.002 on the LB twice; flow2 (velocity denoising) was neutral at 0.947. ILP-chain smoothing also pulls relink decisions toward the in-sample linker (relink-off won locally but lost 0.002 on the LB). The swaps (median length 9.3 um, true link never proposed) are fast movers, not lattice ties, so this does not touch the largest FN class.
hypotheses.not_closed_because: No relink knob changes (gates, bonus and velocity weight are unchanged). It is not the flow prior (no neighbourhood displacement field) and not the global shift. It changes the geometry inputs of every decision stage, which no probe has touched. It is included as the only idea in this set that the CPU lab can test before the GPU capture exists.
